title: A Dream Before Lauds
text: {monk} came to the office before Lauds white-faced, and would not say at first what had troubled him. Then he told the abbot that in the night he had been called by name, and the voice had not sounded like his own.

choices.label: Ask the abbot to hear him
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} told the abbot his dream, and the abbot read in it a calling to be a {monk_path}.

choices.label: Tell him a dream is only a dream
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was told that a dream is only a dream, and he took the advice with a troubled face.

title: A Request for Leave
text: {monk} came to the abbot's door with his hat in his hands and asked leave to go down to the village. There is a girl there, he said, and he believes God means him to marry her.

choices.label: Give him leave and his blessing
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} left the house for the village, and the abbot blessed him at the gate.

choices.label: Ask him to wait a year
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} agreed to wait a year before he spoke again of the village.

title: The Light at Vigil
text: {monk} kept the night vigil alone, as he had asked to, and in the small hours he came to the abbot pale and unsure what he had seen. He would not say it was a sign. He would only say the candle had not gone out, however far he turned from it.

choices.label: Let him tell all he saw
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} told the abbot everything he had seen in the vigil, and the abbot knew him for a {monk_path}.

choices.label: Send him to bed; a candle is only a candle
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was sent to bed, and he slept, or said that he slept.

title: A Confession Over the Ledger
text: {monk} sat down across from the abbot with the account book between them and confessed that for years he had copied more psalms than the house asked for, and kept the spare sheets for himself. He did not say why. He asked only whether that was a sin.

choices.label: Ask what he was making with them
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} said he had been making a book of his own, and the abbot saw in it the work of a {monk_path}.

choices.label: Tell him to return the sheets and say his penance
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} returned the sheets and said his penance without asking why it had been set.

title: Back From the Road
text: {monk} came back from the pilgrim road thinner than he went, and at supper he would not eat until the abbot had said grace twice. When asked what had kept him so long, he said he had been stopped at a ford by a man who knew his name.

choices.label: Ask what the man told him
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} repeated what the man at the ford had told him, and the abbot heard in it the calling of a {monk_path}.

choices.label: Let him rest and say no more of the ford
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} rested, and the ford was not spoken of again in the house.

title: Work Without Words
text: {monk} came back from his amends and went straight out to the fields, where he worked until dark without a word. The steward asked him what he had learned on the road. He said he had learned how to be quiet, and then he asked to be told what he was good for.

choices.label: Tell him to show what he is good for
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} worked the fields as a {monk_path} would, and the steward said so to the abbot.

choices.label: Tell him to keep to the fields
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was set to the fields, and he kept to them without complaint.

title: A Stranger at the Gate
text: A stranger came to the gate asking for {monk} by a name he had not used in years. {monk} went down to meet him and came back a long while later with the look of a man who has been offered something. He would not say what it was.

choices.label: Ask him what was offered
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} told the abbot he had been offered a road, and the abbot saw that it was the road of a {monk_path}.

choices.label: Ask the porter to send the stranger away
choices.chronicle: {When}, the stranger was sent away from the gate, and {monk} did not ask who he was.

title: Nursing a Fever
text: The fever went through the lower cells in a week, and {monk} nursed every brother who took it without sleeping, and with a steadiness nobody had taught him. When the fever broke, the infirmarian asked where he had learned it. {monk} said he had not learned it. He had only known what to do.

choices.label: Ask the infirmarian to set him to the sick
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was set to the sick, and the infirmarian wrote that he had the gift of a {monk_path}.

choices.label: Thank him and send him back to his own work
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} went back to his own work, and the sick were left to the infirmarian.

title: The Bell in the Night
text: {monk} rang the night bell on his own, long after Compline, and when the brothers came down he was kneeling beside it with his hands flat on the bronze. He said the bell had told him to stay. He did not look sorry.

choices.label: Ask what the bell said
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} said the bell had told him to keep vigil for the house, and the abbot named him a {monk_path}.

choices.label: Tell him the bell rings for the hours, not for him
choices.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was told that the bell rings for the hours and not for him, and he took it humbly.
